 Bolivar Central Driver License Event Issues 21 Permits 
 November 12, 2026 at 5:35 pm CST 
 Jon Ross Myers 
 A school-based driver license event at Bolivar Central High School helped Hardeman County students get learner permits, REAL IDs and new driver licenses without a trip to a state testing center. The “Keys to Unlock Your Future” event was a partnership between the Ayers Foundation Trust and the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, The Magnolia Post reported on Nov. 12.
 What the Driver License Event Accomplished
 State examiners brought their services to the Bolivar Central campus so students could finish paperwork and testing during the school day. According to the report, the event produced:
 21 learner permits
 9 road tests, with 7 students earning new driver licenses
 15 REAL ID credentials
 2 duplicate credentials
 8 new organ donor registrations
 1 new voter registration
 The exact date of the event was not given, and the report said only that it was held recently.
 Why a Permit or License Matters for Students
 For many teenagers in rural West Tennessee, a driver license is more than a milestone. It can be the key to a first job, dual-enrollment classes, college visits and family responsibilities. In a rural county, many families live miles from the nearest testing center. Getting to an appointment can mean missed work for a parent and missed class for a student.
 Bringing the testing to the school removes much of that barrier. The partners said the goal was to help students move toward independence and give them tools they will need as they look for new opportunities after high school.
 Ayers Foundation’s Work in Hardeman County Schools
 The Ayers Foundation Trust is active across Hardeman County Schools, which include Middleton High School. Earlier this month, Tippah News reported on an Ayers Foundation visit at Middleton High focused on college and career access. The foundation is known in West Tennessee for placing counselors in high schools to help students with college applications, financial aid and career planning.
 The Bolivar Central event shows how those partnerships can reach practical needs, too. A REAL ID, a learner permit or a road test can be the first step toward the jobs and training programs counselors help students pursue.
 What Families Should Know About REAL ID
 REAL ID-compliant credentials are marked with a star and are required for boarding domestic flights and entering certain federal facilities. Tennessee issues them through the Department of Safety and Homeland Security. Families in Middleton and across Hardeman County who missed this event can check the department’s website for driver services locations, required documents and appointment options.
 Students interested in future school-based events should ask their school counselor whether another session is planned.
